commit_message:
Bug 1928666 part 4 - Support nursery-allocated buffer for Map/Set objects. r=jonco

This changes how the buffer is allocated/freed to be more similar to other objects with
nursery-allocated buffers. The finalizer is no longer called for nursery `Map`/`Set`
objects but we rely on the nursery's malloc buffer handling instead.

Nursery-allocating this buffer is a large speedup. We just have to fix up the hash table
chains after moving the buffer in memory.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D228981

fix_commit.message: Bug 1970095 - Clean up some Map/Set code. r=iain
fix_commit.author: Jan de Mooij

findings.title: Integer truncation from size_t to uint32_t in buffer allocation
findings.message: The allocateCellBuffer function accepts a size_t numBytes parameter but passes it directly to AllocateCellBuffer<uint8_t>() which expects a uint32_t count parameter. When allocating buffers for very large Map/Set objects, the size can exceed UINT32_MAX (4GB), causing the value to be truncated to a much smaller 32-bit value. This results in allocating a significantly undersized buffer. Subsequently, when the Map/Set is rehashed (during OrderedHashTableImpl::rehash), memcpy operations copy data based on the expected larger size, but write to the smaller allocated buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow.
findings.suggestion: Add a maximum size limit for Map/Set entries to prevent the buffer size from exceeding values that can be safely represented in 32 bits. Alternatively, change the AllocateCellBuffer family of functions to accept size_t parameters instead of uint32_t.

findings.title: Missing size validation in allocateBuffer allows overflow
findings.message: The allocateBuffer function calculates numBytes using calcAllocSize which can produce very large size_t values. While calcAllocSize uses CheckedInt to detect overflow within size_t, there is no check that the resulting size fits within uint32_t before passing to allocateCellBuffer. This allows the code path to proceed with a truncated size value when the actual required buffer exceeds 4GB.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit check that numBytes fits within the range expected by allocateCellBuffer, or add capacity limits to prevent the hash table from growing to sizes that would cause overflow.

ground_truth.root_cause: Type mismatch between the size_t used in OrderedHashTableObject.allocateCellBuffer() and the uint32_t expected by the GC's AllocateCellBuffer<T>() template function. The GC allocation functions were designed with the assumption that object buffers would never exceed 4GB, but no validation was added when the Map/Set code started using these functions for nursery-allocated buffers.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable type conversion where size_t numBytes parameter is passed to AllocateCellBuffer<uint8_t>() which expects uint32_t, causing integer truncation when numBytes exceeds UINT32_MAX (4GB). This is the point where the dangerous implicit cast from 64-bit to 32-bit occurs without validation.
